data.name: Antiflux
data.detailed_description:
Robots, teleporters, jump pads, lasers! Be prepared for an action-filled challenging puzzle experience! Antiflux an oldschool-style puzzle platformer. Puzzles are complex but easy to understand. The platforming is simple but fun, controls comfortably with a touch screen or controller. Pick up upgrades along your journey recover lost research on an abandoned planet, and discover its dark secrets!

Features:
  • Puzzle-platformer with oldschool game design.
  • Interesting mechanics and puzzles.
  • Over 60 well designed levels.
  • Complexity building permanent upgrades.
  • Runs on Vertex Engine 7 - Custom built OpenGL ES2 engine.
  • Full controller support.
  • Atmospheric original soundtrack.

data.short_description: Antiflux is a challenging but fun puzzle platformer with upgrades, building complexity over time.

reviews.review:
Antiflux is a focused puzzle platformer that builds its appeal around environmental challenges rather than constant combat or elaborate storytelling. Developed and published by UAA Software, the game places the player on an abandoned planet where recovering lost research gradually leads to the discovery of secrets hidden within the environment. Its science-fiction premise is deliberately straightforward, allowing the puzzles and platforming mechanics to remain the central attraction throughout the experience.

The gameplay revolves around navigating carefully constructed stages filled with mechanisms such as teleporters, jump pads, lasers, robots, switches, and other obstacles. Movement itself is relatively simple to understand, but reaching the destination can require considerably more thought. Each room encourages players to examine the environment, understand how its components interact, and determine the correct sequence of actions. Some solutions become obvious after studying the layout, while others demand experimentation and repeated attempts before everything falls into place.

Progression becomes more interesting through permanent upgrades that expand what the player can accomplish. These abilities are not merely rewards for advancing through the game. They become important parts of increasingly complicated puzzles. Early stages introduce concepts individually, while later areas combine established mechanics in ways that require greater precision and planning. This gradual layering of ideas helps prevent the puzzle design from becoming repetitive, especially as familiar devices can serve different purposes depending on the surrounding level configuration.

With more than 60 levels, Antiflux provides a respectable amount of material for a relatively modest puzzle game. The level-based structure allows individual challenges to remain focused instead of forcing puzzles into a large interconnected environment. Difficulty rises as the player advances, with later sections expecting a stronger understanding of movement, timing, upgrades, and environmental interactions. Trial and error is sometimes necessary, particularly when several mechanisms need to be activated in the correct order. This can produce occasional frustration, but solving a troublesome room after understanding its underlying logic is also one of the game's most satisfying qualities.

The presentation favors functionality over visual extravagance. Its abandoned science-fiction environments establish an appropriately lonely atmosphere while keeping important gameplay elements readable. Lasers, machines, platforms, and other interactive objects are generally more important than decorative scenery, which suits a game where quickly interpreting a room can be essential. The original soundtrack further supports the isolated atmosphere without distracting from puzzle solving. The overall presentation may feel basic compared with more elaborate modern platformers, but its simplicity complements the game's old-school personality.

Storytelling remains secondary to gameplay. The search for missing research gives the player a reason to continue deeper into the abandoned world, while hints of darker secrets add some mystery to the journey. Players expecting extensive conversations, cinematic sequences, or detailed character development will find the narrative relatively restrained. Instead, the setting functions mainly as context for moving between challenges. This works reasonably well because Antiflux clearly prioritizes mechanical progression and environmental problem-solving over narrative complexity.

Controller support is another welcome feature for a game built around platforming. Its lightweight technical requirements also make it approachable on relatively modest hardware. Steam Deck compatibility, however, does not have an official Valve Verified or Playable rating listed for the game, so its Steam Deck status should be considered Unknown or Unverified. The modest system requirements suggest that performance demands should not be the primary concern, but an unverified status means players should not assume completely seamless handheld operation, controller mapping, interface readability, or compatibility without testing it themselves.

Antiflux works best for players who enjoy compact games that introduce straightforward mechanics and then steadily find more demanding ways to combine them. It does not rely on visual spectacle, huge environments, or complex combat systems to maintain interest. Instead, teleportation, hazards, movement tools, permanent upgrades, and increasingly elaborate level arrangements form the foundation of the experience. The presentation and narrative are relatively modest, but the puzzle design has enough variety to give the game its own identity.

Taken as a complete package, Antiflux is a worthwhile old-school puzzle platformer with a clear understanding of its priorities. Its collection of more than 60 stages gives its mechanics room to develop, while the progression system helps keep later puzzles from simply repeating earlier concepts. Some players may find the presentation dated or the more difficult challenges frustrating, but anyone who enjoys methodically studying a level and discovering the intended solution should find plenty to appreciate. UAA Software created a small-scale experience that succeeds through mechanical focus rather than unnecessary complexity.

Rating: 8/10
